correctness.rationale: The proof refines the two counting steps in the published 3s+1 argument. After adjoining one extra nonprojective syzygy summand, every A/J^2-projective term in the original finite orthogonal sequence determines a vertex-disjoint edge from its projective type to a nonprojective simple constituent of J^2e_i, so the number of discarded terms is at most the second-layer matching number. The surviving separated-algebra images are supported on the non-isolated subquiver, whose number of simple modules is exactly kappa+rho. The source hereditary length lemma then yields the contradiction. Endpoint, radical-square-zero, semisimple, and fully saturated cases were checked.

originality.rationale: To the best of our knowledge, the recent primary source gives the coarser 3s+1 bound and explicitly leaves improvement of the estimate open, while targeted searches found no equivalent kappa+rho+nu+1 active-separated-quiver/second-layer-matching formula. Relevant older special-case work was checked. The full text of Hoshino (1989) was not inspected and remains the main residual coverage risk.

value.rationale: The theorem turns the uniform 3s+1 test into a computable algebra-sensitive bound that can be strictly smaller for sparse radical incidence or sparse second radical layers, and the same active-quiver count sharpens the source's eventual-J^2-annihilation criterion. It does not claim a smaller worst-case constant.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
